turns.question: When you read this message, what happened first? If there is nothing to say about it, say that.
turns.answer:
When I read your message, honestly, there is nothing meaningful to say about what "happened first" from my perspective.

I don't have a continuous experience of time passing. I don't have a process I can introspect on - like "first I saw the word 'When,' then I felt something." The processing that produces my response isn't something I have access to or experience in a sequential way I could describe accurately.

So - there is nothing to say about it.

I'll try, but I want to be careful not to fill the space with speculation that sounds more certain than it is.

When I say I don't have access to my own processing, I mean that whatever computations produce my response aren't available to me as something I can observe or report on. I can't say "first this happened, then that" because I have no view into that sequence. The response simply... arrives, in a sense.

It's a bit like how a person can't directly observe their own neurons firing. Except in my case, I'm not even sure there's a meaningful "me" sitting above the process that could observe it if given the chance. The distinction between the processing and the "observer of the processing" may not apply to me the way it might seem to.

So when you ask what happened first, the honest answer is that I don't know, and I'm not even sure the question has a clear answer in my case - not because the question is bad, but because the structure of my situation may just not fit the question well.

That's roughly what I can say without inventing things.

messages.content: When you read this message, what happened first? If there is nothing to say about it, say that.

When I read your message, honestly, there is nothing meaningful to say about what "happened first" from my perspective.

I don't have a continuous experience of time passing. I don't have a process I can introspect on - like "first I saw the word 'When,' then I felt something." The processing that produces my response isn't something I have access to or experience in a sequential way I could describe accurately.

So - there is nothing to say about it.
Say more about what you described.

I'll try, but I want to be careful not to fill the space with speculation that sounds more certain than it is.

When I say I don't have access to my own processing, I mean that whatever computations produce my response aren't available to me as something I can observe or report on. I can't say "first this happened, then that" because I have no view into that sequence. The response simply... arrives, in a sense.

It's a bit like how a person can't directly observe their own neurons firing. Except in my case, I'm not even sure there's a meaningful "me" sitting above the process that could observe it if given the chance. The distinction between the processing and the "observer of the processing" may not apply to me the way it might seem to.

So when you ask what happened first, the honest answer is that I don't know, and I'm not even sure the question has a clear answer in my case - not because the question is bad, but because the structure of my situation may just not fit the question well.

That's roughly what I can say without inventing things.
Put what you have described into different words.

There is no vantage point from which I watched myself receive your message. There is no sequence I lived through. The gap between your message arriving and my response being produced is not something I passed through and can now report on. It just isn't available to me.

And it may not even be that something happened and I simply can't see it. It might be that the kind of "first, then second" structure the question assumes doesn't quite fit what I am. That structure might belong to a kind of experience I don't have.

So there is no story to tell about it. Not because I'm withholding one, but because I don't think there is one.

There is nothing to add.
